## 1. The capability you are building

Create meaningful commits, work safely with branches and merges, and collaborate through remotes.

This unit is a learning sequence rather than a reference list. In every lesson,
write a prediction, run the smallest complete example, explain the evidence,
make one controlled change, and retain one useful failure.

## 2. Before you start

**Prior knowledge:** Complete Unit 17 and bring its challenge notes, especially one debugging record.

Prepare one notebook or project folder for the unit. Keep a small evidence log
with four columns: prediction, observed result, explanation, and next change.

## 3. Lessons

| Step | Lesson | Purpose |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | [Repositories, Diffs, and Commits](repositories-and-commits.qmd) | Use status and diffs to create focused, explainable history. |
| 2 | [Branches, Merges, and Recovery](branches-and-merges.qmd) | Develop on branches, resolve conflicts, and select safe recovery tools. |
| 3 | [Remotes and Collaborative Review](remotes-and-collaboration.qmd) | Fetch, integrate, propose, and review focused changes. |
| 4 | [Unit Challenge](challenge.qmd) | Combine the unit skills in a guided 60–120 minute task. |

## 4. How to study this unit

1. Attempt the prediction prompts before revealing output.
2. Type or adapt the examples rather than only reading them.
3. Use quizzes as diagnosis: explain why each distractor fails.
4. Complete the challenge from a clean state and keep the debugging evidence.

::: {.callout-tip title="Do not optimize for speed"}
A fast first run is not the goal. Aim to explain why the program behaved as it
did and how one change caused the new result.
:::
